title: Grey Walter's tortoises: first autonomous robots

research.what: Neurophysiologist W. Grey Walter built small analogue-electronic robots with two valve 'neurons' to test how simple neural circuits could produce lifelike, exploratory behaviour. Origin: W. Grey Walter's Elmer and Elsie tortoises, Burden Neurological Institute, Bristol, 1948-49

change.what: Elmer and Elsie roamed freely, steered toward light, reacted to obstacles by touch and returned to recharge, so they are generally regarded as the first electronic autonomous robots with complex behaviour.

note: They founded behaviour-based robotics and are cited as ancestors of Roomba-style robots, and Walter's 1950s successors were shown to the public at the 1951 Festival of Britain.

refs.label: University of Bristol: Grey Walter and his tortoises
IEEE Spectrum: Meet the Roomba's Ancestor, the Cybernetic Tortoise

security.note: Hard-wired analogue control had no software or network link, so it had no cyber attack surface.

title: Amazon DeepFleet: foundation model coordinating warehouse robots

research.what: Amazon Robotics trained a suite of multi-agent foundation models on fleet movement data from hundreds of thousands of warehouse robots, to forecast and coordinate fleet movement. Origin: Amazon Robotics technical report 'DeepFleet: Multi-Agent Foundation Models for Mobile Robots', arXiv 2508.08574, August 2025.

change.what: Amazon announced around 30 June to 1 July 2025 that DeepFleet was in use to route its robot fleet across more than 300 sites, with a claimed 10% gain in robot travel efficiency.

note: One of the first foundation models used in production to coordinate a very large mobile-robot fleet.

refs.label: Robotics 24/7: Amazon launches AI foundation model to power its robotic fleet

security.note: A single learned model steering a fleet of over a million robots creates one central point whose compromise or corrupted training data could disrupt operations.
